steps.title: Open the dashboard
steps.narration: Trendora opens straight to today's market read — no sign-in required, and every card fills in with real numbers right away.
steps.point_out: The Market Regime card reads "Risk-on 65.98/100" and the Market Phase & Severity card shows "Expansion" — both settle in well under a second.

steps.title: Tuck away the regime x phase chart
steps.narration: Further down the page, a "Regime x phase cross-view" chart lines up index performance against the market's phase history — you can hide it any time you don't need it.
steps.point_out: Clicking Hide collapses the whole chart down to a single small toggle button.

steps.title: Bring the chart back — now noticeably snappier
steps.narration: Clicking it again reloads the chart on demand. This iteration's fix shaved its real-browser load time from over two seconds down to under one, so the wait barely registers.
steps.point_out: The full two-pane chart reappears, already labeled with its as-of date.

steps.title: Open Data Manager
steps.narration: Data Manager tracks exactly how much price history and how many daily snapshots are on hand, including a calendar heatmap of coverage over time.
steps.point_out: The coverage heatmap and its color-coded legend now finish loading well inside their speed budget too.

steps.title: Fill in a backfill start date
steps.narration: In the "Start a fetch / backfill job" panel, you can queue a backfill for any date range directly from the browser.

steps.title: Fill in the end date
steps.narration: Rounding out the range with an end date is all it takes to define the job.

steps.title: Run the backfill
steps.narration: Clicking Start kicks the job off immediately — this particular range covers two weekend days, so there's no real data to fetch.
steps.point_out: The job finishes right away and honestly reports "2 non-trading" days rather than pretending it did work.

steps.title: Check the run history stays honest
steps.narration: Reloading the page and scrolling to Run history shows exactly what happened — a zero-work run is never dressed up as a normal success.
steps.point_out: The newest row carries a distinct grey "no new snapshots" badge instead of the green "ok" badge a real data-producing run gets.
